chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I said to Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: I stand in salat (prayer) and see excrement before me in the direction of the qiblah. He said: “Move away from it as much as you can, and do not perform salat (prayer) on the roadways.”

And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: There is no harm in a person performing salat (prayer) while wearing a sheathed sword, or with a knife in its sheath in his sleeve, or other than that of iron, if he needs to keep it with him. And if he performs salat (prayer) while on his finger there is a ring made of iron, that does not harm him, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act being discussed
key_terms.الْحَدِيدِ: iron items mentioned in relation to prayer
key_terms.الْعَذِرَةَ: excrement or filth seen in front of the worshipper

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) near impurity or while carrying iron items such as a sword or ring?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses legal rulings related to salat (prayer) concerning the prayer place and items carried during prayer. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs avoiding impurity in front of the worshipper as much as possible and forbids praying on public roadways, while al-Shaykh adds that carrying iron items when needed does not invalidate the prayer.
